memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Early the next morning Jacob took the stone he had placed under his head and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on top of it. He called that place Bethel, though the city used to be called Luz." - Gen 28:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob does not simply move on and forget his encounter with God. He takes the very stone that had been his hard pillow, sets it up as a pillar, pours oil over it, and names the place Bethel — "the house of God." The place where he felt most alone became a landmark of God's faithfulness. The stone of his hardship became a monument of grace.

There is wisdom in marking our encounters with God. Our memories are short, and in the rush of life we easily forget the moments when God met us, spoke to us, or carried us through. Jacob built a marker so he would never forget that God had been there.

We can do the same in our own way — writing down answered prayers, keeping a journal of God's faithfulness, remembering the day He met us in our need. These "stones" become anchors for our faith. When doubt or hardship comes later, we can look back and say, "God was faithful there; He will be faithful again."

Notice too that the stone of Jacob's discomfort became the very symbol of blessing. God has a way of transforming our hard places into holy ground. What is the "stone" in your story that God has turned into a Bethel? Do not forget it — mark it, and give thanks.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I remember and mark the times God has met me?
2. What "hard stone" in my life has God turned into a place of blessing?
3. Would keeping a record of God's faithfulness strengthen my faith?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me never to forget the moments You have met me. Turn the hard places of my life into holy ground, and keep my heart full of grateful remembrance. Amen.
